canonical_concept.beeja: हं (Haṃ) — the bīja of the space element (ākāśa) in Tantric traditions. Associated with the Viśuddha chakra (throat — the space center).
canonical_concept.vyakarana: Ākāśa is a masculine noun derived from the prefix ā- and the root kāś (to shine). The word conveys both the sense of "space" and "luminosity" — space is not empty but luminous.
canonical_concept.functional_meaning: Ākāśa is the subtlest of the five elements — the space in which all other elements and all phenomena exist. It is the medium of sound (śabda) — sound travels through ākāśa. In Vedānta, ākāśa is the first element to emerge from Brahman in the process of creation. The Chāndogya Upaniṣad teaches that Brahman is ākāśa — the infinite space of consciousness.
canonical_concept.dhatu: आ + काश् (Ā + Kāś) — Ā (towards, completely) + Kāś (to shine, to be luminous). That which shines completely; the luminous space.
canonical_concept.nirukta: "Ākāśate iti ākāśaḥ" — that which shines. Space is not mere emptiness but the luminous ground of all existence.
canonical_concept.tattva: Ākāśa-Tattva — the space principle. The first and subtlest of the five mahābhūtas (great elements): Ākāśa (space), Vāyu (air), Agni (fire), Āp (water), Pṛthvī (earth). Ākāśa is the substratum of all other elements — they all exist within space.
